messages.content:
Spiritual Weapon 2nd Level • Evocation

You create a floating, spectral weapon within range that lasts for the duration or until you cast this spell again. When you cast the spell, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of the weapon. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the weapon up to 20 feet and repeat the attack against a creature within 5 feet of it.

The weapon can take whatever form you choose. Clerics of deities who are associated with a particular weapon (as St. Cuthbert is known for his mace and Thor for his hammer) make this spell's effect resemble that weapon.

At Higher Levels.

When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for every two slot levels above 2nd.

messages.content:
Odkupienie Pythora
This mighty weapon was crafted by Orion Xul and Volkan, God of Forges in legendary Mithral Forge.

Immediately after you make a ranged attack with this weapon, it flies back to your hand.
Whenever you roll a 20 on your attack roll with this weapon, each creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target takes 5 lightning damage.
You gain a +11d20+1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using this weapon. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra 1d61d6 lightning damage.

Fated EnhancementsPythor's Redemption was further improved by a deal with the Fates, into which the Demgod wove threads of their own manhood.

The weapon’s bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +21d20+2, and the extra lightning damage dealt by the weapon increases to 2d62d6.
As an action, you can unleash a 30-foot cone of destructive energy from the weapon. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d68d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this action is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

Shield Wall
action
You can use a bonus action to activate your Shield Wall ability. You may use this ability once, and you regain the ability to do so after completing a long rest. For 1 minute, you and every ally who can see or hear you gains +21d20+2 AC as long as they are standing within 5 feet of an ally who is using a shield. Additionally, your allies wielding shields gain an additional +11d20+1 AC from their own shields (this includes you).

messages.content:
Axe of Xander
This is a sentient, lawful neutral +21d20+2 greataxe (Intelligence 14, Wisdom 10, Charisma 10). It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 120 feet. It communicates empathically by transmitting emotion to the creature carrying or using it.
The axe’s primary purpose is to destroy giants and titans. When you attack one of those creatures you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. When attacking giants or titans Axe of Xander also deals an extra 2d62d6 force damage. It also transmits a tremendous sense of satisfaction and wellbeing to its user when it kills a giant or titan. You may heal 2d102d10 Hit Points when this happens.
This greataxe has 9 charges. As long as the weapon has at least 1 charge, attacks you make with it deal an extra 1d61d6 force damage to any target it hits. When you score a critical hit on an attack roll made with this weapon, it regains 3 expended charges.
Forceful Slash. When you take the Attack action using this axe, you can forgo one of your attacks to expend 3 or more of the greataxe's charges to slash the air in front you. When you do, a 30-foot cone of force emits from the blade. Creatures within range must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d61d6 force damage for each expended charge. If you expend 4 or more charges in this way and leave the Axe of Xander with 0 remaining charges, the weapon realses even more powerful wave of force. When it happens, targets within the area of effect take an extra 3d63d6 force damage, and creatures that succeed on the Dexterity saving throw take half damage instead of avoiding the effect, creatures that fail on the Dexterity Saving Throw are knocked prone. The DC for this property's saving throw is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + the number of charges you expend.

messages.content:
Polymorph 4th Level • Transmutation

This spell transforms a creature that you can see within range into a new form. An unwilling creature must make a Wisdom saving throw to avoid the effect. The spell has no effect on a shapechanger or a creature with 0 hit points.

The transformation lasts for the duration, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. The new form can be any beast whose challenge rating is equal to or less than the target's (or the target's level, if it doesn't have a challenge rating). The target's game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast. It retains its alignment and personality.

The target assumes the hit points of its new form. When it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the number of hit points it had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hit points, it isn't knocked unconscious.

The creature is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can't speak, cast spells, or take any other action that requires hands or speech.

The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment.

Materials a caterpillar cocoon

messages.content:
Axe of Xander
This is a sentient, lawful neutral +21d20+2 greataxe (Intelligence 14, Wisdom 10, Charisma 10). It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 120 feet. It communicates empathically by transmitting emotion to the creature carrying or using it.
The axe’s primary purpose is to destroy giants and titans. When you attack one of those creatures you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. When attacking giants or titans Axe of Xander also deals an extra 2d62d6 force damage. It also transmits a tremendous sense of satisfaction and wellbeing to its user when it kills a giant or titan. You may heal 2d102d10 Hit Points when this happens.
This greataxe has 9 charges. As long as the weapon has at least 1 charge, attacks you make with it deal an extra 1d61d6 force damage to any target it hits. When you score a critical hit on an attack roll made with this weapon, it regains 3 expended charges.
Forceful Slash. When you take the Attack action using this axe, you can forgo one of your attacks to expend 3 or more of the greataxe's charges to slash the air in front you. When you do, a 30-foot cone of force emits from the blade. Creatures within range must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d61d6 force damage for each expended charge. If you expend 4 or more charges in this way and leave the Axe of Xander with 0 remaining charges, the weapon realses even more powerful wave of force. When it happens, targets within the area of effect take an extra 3d63d6 force damage, and creatures that succeed on the Dexterity saving throw take half damage instead of avoiding the effect, creatures that fail on the Dexterity Saving Throw are knocked prone. The DC for this property's saving throw is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + the number of charges you expend.

messages.content:
Telamok Funeral Mask
Wondrous item, Uncommon
This funeral mask is made of bronze, formed to the shape of a dead man’s face. While wearing the mask you can cast disguise self at will, but only to assume the form of the humanoid in whose image the mask was formed. You can place the mask on a humanoid corpse for one minute to form the mask to their face.
If the mask has been placed on a corpse for five minutes, you can ask the corpse up to three questions. This fails to work if the corpse has already been affected by the mask, or a similar effect such as the speak with dead spell. The corpse knows only what it knew in life, including the languages it knew. Answers are usually brief, cryptic, or repetitive, and the corpse is under no compulsion to offer a truthful answer if you are hostile to it or it recognizes you as an enemy. The corpse can’t learn new information, doesn’t comprehend anything that has happened since it died, and can’t speculate about future events. Its voice comes as muffled whispers from behind the bronze mask.

messages.content:
Polymorph
Legacy • 4th Level Transmutation (Cast at 4th Level)
Casting Time1 action
Durationup to 1 hour
ComponentsV, S, M(a caterpillar cocoon)
Range60ft.
ConcentrationRequires Concentration
This spell transforms a creature that you can see within range into a new form. An unwilling creature must make a Wisdom saving throw to avoid the effect. The spell has no effect on a shapechanger or a creature with 0 hit points.
The transformation lasts for the duration, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. The new form can be any beast whose challenge rating is equal to or less than the target's (or the target's level, if it doesn't have a challenge rating). The target's game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast. It retains its alignment and personality.
The target assumes the hit points of its new form. When it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the number of hit points it had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hit points, it isn't knocked unconscious.
The creature is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can't speak, cast spells, or take any other action that requires hands or speech.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment.
